title: Spin-Polarized Weyl Fermions and Unconventional Spin Transport
authors: Chenhao Liang, Haohao Sheng, Sheng Zhang, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, Zhijun Wang
abstract: Large and electrically controllable spin splitting in nonmagnetic materials is highly desirable for condensed-matter physics and spintronics, enabling strongly spin-polarized quasiparticles and unconventional spin transport as well as their electrical control. Here, we establish a general framework for critical spin-polarized Weyl fermions in two-dimensional (2D) nonmagnetic systems. We predict the $α$-Bi-like Group-V puckered-layer family of 2D ferroelectrics as a material platform combining critical spin-Weyl fermions, giant spin splitting, and electrically switchable nonlinear and spin transport. Our calculations reveal exchange-scale spin splitting induced by spin-orbit coupling and a $p$-wave spin texture in the BiAs monolayer. Moreover, BiAs hosts four critical spin-Weyl points, each formed within a single-spin channel. The nearly quantized $\langle S_z\rangle$ is protected by an emergent $S_z$-conservation symmetry in the low-energy limit. The spin-Weyl cones also give rise to unconventional spin-transport phenomena, including a purely out-of-plane Edelstein response and a pronounced spin Nernst effect. Ferroelectric reversal further enables electrical switching of the $p$-wave spin texture and inversion-odd responses, while the tunability of these properties through composition, strain, and magnetic field is also systematically demonstrated across the entire family. These results establish both a general nonmagnetic framework and a promising material platform for exploring critical spin-Weyl physics, nonlinear Hall phenomena, and unconventional spin transport.
summary: This work develops a general theory for critical spin-Weyl fermions in 2D nonmagnetic ferroelectrics, identifying the $\alpha$-Bi-like family as a promising material class. Through theoretical calculations, the authors predict giant spin splitting and novel spin transport effects, which can be actively controlled by reversing the material's ferroelectric polarization.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a general theoretical framework for critical spin-polarized Weyl fermions in 2D nonmagnetic systems and identify a viable material platform exhibiting unconventional spin transport.
main_result: The $\alpha$-Bi-like Group-V ferroelectric family, specifically BiAs, was shown to host critical spin-Weyl points, giant spin splitting, and electrically switchable nonlinear/spin transport phenomena.
method: The study uses first-principles calculations combined with the construction of an effective k.p Hamiltonian derived from symmetry analysis to model the electronic structure and transport properties.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a four-band k.p Hamiltonian for 2D nonmagnetic ferroelectrics. The focus is on the $\alpha$-Bi-like puckered-layer family, with BiAs serving as the primary example.
key_observables: Spin splitting magnitude, spin Chern numbers ($C_s$), Berry curvature dipole ($D_{yz}$), out-of-plane Edelstein response, and Spin Nernst conductivity ($	ext{SNC}$).
important_parameters: Electric field/Ferroelectric polarization (for switching), strain, and magnetic field strength.
main_assumptions: The low-energy physics is described by an effective k.p Hamiltonian, and the analysis relies on symmetry constraints to protect certain spin components.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the odd-wave spin textures, topological phase diagrams showing the evolution of spin Chern numbers, and calculations demonstrating how ferroelectric reversal switches the sign of the Berry curvature dipole and spin texture.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the general symmetry conditions for critical spin-Weyl fermions. It then applies this framework to the $\alpha$-Bi-like family, calculating band structures, topological invariants, and various transport coefficients (like BCD and $	ext{SNC}$) to demonstrate the predicted phenomena.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the concept of symmetry-protected topological states and the ability to electrically switch fundamental electronic properties (like spin texture) is highly relevant to engineered quantum materials and controlling quantum states.
